import subprocess, re, json

def parse_pdf(path):
    text = subprocess.run(["pdftotext", path, "-"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    blocks = re.split(r'<code=(PHY\d+)>', text)
    questions = []
    for i in range(1, len(blocks), 2):
        code = blocks[i]
        rest = blocks[i+1]
        meta = re.search(r'<lvl=([^>]+)><part=([^>]+)><type=([^>]+)><mark=(\d+)><bk=(\d+)><ch=(\d+)>', rest)
        content_m = re.search(r'<content>\s*\n?(.*?)(?:-- ans|$)', rest, re.DOTALL)
        content = content_m.group(1).strip() if content_m else ""
        # clean content
        content = re.sub(r'«+', '', content)
        content = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', content)[:200]
        lvl = meta.group(1) if meta else "?"
        questions.append({"code": code, "num": int(code[-2:]), "lvl": lvl, "preview": content})
    return questions

for fname in ["4_ch02_MC_e.pdf", "4_ch02_MC_e_answer.pdf"]:
    path = f"/Users/sinchunyeung/Documents-local/Materials/Phy/qb/QB_402/{fname}"
    qs = parse_pdf(path)
    print(f"\n{fname}: {len(qs)} questions")
    for q in qs:
        print(f"  Q{q['num']:02d} [{q['lvl']}] {q['code']}: {q['preview'][:120]}")

## Source notes

| File | Result |
|------|--------|
| `active-physics/Book 4.pdf` | Image-based (no embedded text). Section order recovered by OCR on Ch. 21 (*Circuit and Power* / electric circuits). |
| `notes/Book-4.pdf` | **Not found** (empty `notes/` folder). |
| `qb/QB_402/4_ch02_MC_e.pdf` | 32 questions (Q39–Q70 only). |
| `qb/QB_402/4_ch02_MC_e_answer.pdf` | Full bank: **70 questions** (Q1–Q70). |

**Numbering:** Textbook = **Ch. 21** (*Circuit and Power*); QB metadata = `bk=4, ch=02`. Your “Section 3” = **§21.3 Resistance**.

---

## Book 4 teaching order — from §21.3 onwards

### **§21.3 Resistance**
**Covers:** \(R=V/I\), ohm (Ω); Ohm’s law vs ohmic/non-ohmic; straight vs curved \(I\)–\(V\) graphs; \(R=\rho L/A\) (length, area/diameter); variable resistor/rheostat; temperature effects (metal vs semiconductor); filament bulb, thermistor, LDR; voltmeter–ammeter method to find \(R\).

| QB MC | Topic |
|-------|-------|
| **Q7** | Composite rods (different \(d\), \(\ell\)) — series resistors |
| **Q13** | Statements about Ohm’s law / ohmic devices |
| **Q16** | Definition of ohmic device |
| **Q18** | Straight \(V=IR\) calculation |
| **Q22** | Brightness when adding series/parallel resistor |
| **Q34, Q35, Q42** | Wire dimensions → resistance scaling |
| **Q43** | Tungsten wire under large constant \(V\) (heating, non-ohmic) |
| **Q44, Q45, Q46** | \(I\)–\(V\) experiments; resistance from graph; \(R(T)\) |
| **Q56, Q57** | LDR in circuit — \(I\) or \(V\) vs brightness graphs |

---

### **§21.4 Resistor networks**
**Covers:** Series vs parallel (same \(I\) vs same \(V\)); \(R_{\mathrm{eq}}\) rules; stepwise reduction; identical-resistor tricks; Kirchhoff/current splitting; potential dividers; opposing cells; switch effects; burnt filament = open branch; variable resistor loading a network.

| QB MC | Topic |
|-------|-------|
| **Q1** | Three-bulb network — \(I\), \(V\), energy/power ratios |
| **Q2** | Place given resistors so two ammeters match |
| **Q3** | Electron energy change in identical-resistor network |
| **Q4** | Voltmeter between different points (\(X\)–\(Y\) vs \(X\)–\(Z\)) |
| **Q5, Q6** | Identical-resistor networks → battery \(I\) or e.m.f. |
| **Q8** | Power in parallel branches (identical \(R\)) |
| **Q9** | Variable resistor — ammeter & voltmeter readings |
| **Q10** | Parallel branches — relate \(I_1,I_2,I_3\) |
| **Q11** | Compare two equivalent networks P vs Q |
| **Q14, Q15** | Ammeter readings — series vs parallel junctions |
| **Q19, Q20, Q21** | Simple \(6\,\mathrm{V}\) series pair — \(I\) and \(V\) on one resistor |
| **Q36, Q37** | Two switches — voltmeter reading (open/short paths) |
| **Q38** | Mixed \(1\,\Omega/2\,\Omega/4\,\Omega\) — branch current |
| **Q39** | Burnt filament — which bulbs stay lit |
| **Q41** | Two bulbs — compare \(V\) across each |
| **Q47** | Many ammeters in network — find incorrect statement |
| **Q48** | Closing switch — ammeter changes |
| **Q49** | Four identical bulbs — brightness statements |
| **Q50** | Two switches — ammeter reading |
| **Q51** | Three identical \(R\), \(1\,\mathrm{V}\) cell |
| **Q52** | Opposing \(6\,\mathrm{V}\) + \(12\,\mathrm{V}\) cells |
| **Q53** | Equivalent resistance between P and Q |
| **Q54, Q55, Q70** | Resistance ratios → \(V\) ratios or \(I\) ratios |
| **Q68, Q69** | Mixed \(R_1:R_2:R_3=1:2:3\) — power or series/parallel power comparison |

---

### **§21.5 Electrical power**
**Covers:** \(P=VI=I^2R=V^2/R\); energy \(E=Pt\); brightness \(\propto P\); heating effect; power in series (\(P\propto R\) at fixed \(I\)) vs parallel (\(P\propto 1/R\) at fixed \(V\)); battery capacity (A·h); which arrangement drains slowest.

| QB MC | Topic |
|-------|-------|
| **Q12** | Power scaling — change \(R\) and e.m.f. |
| **Q40** | Laptop battery — voltage, capacity, energy |
| **Q58** | Valid power unit (VA) |
| **Q59, Q60, Q63** | Variable resistor — power in branch vs whole circuit |
| **Q61** | Three series resistors — \(P\) ratio |
| **Q62** | Mixed lamps + fixed resistor — total power |
| **Q64** | \(n\) identical bulbs in series — total power |
| **Q65, Q66** | Parallel/mixed lamp networks — power ratios |
| **Q67** | Three-lamp + two-cell setups — longest run time |

---

### **Short circuit & open circuit** *(Book 4: after §21.5, before §21.6)*
**Covers:** Ideal wire bypasses load; shorted bulb/battery; open = broken path, \(I=0\); danger of large \(I\); switch creating a short across a resistor.

| QB MC | Topic |
|-------|-------|
| **Q36, Q37** | Switch combinations — voltmeter reads 0 or full e.m.f. |
| **Q48** | Switch shorts a parallel branch — ammeter response |
| **Q39** | Open circuit from burnt filament |

---

### **§21.6 Internal resistance**
**Covers:** Real cell = e.m.f. \(\mathcal{E}\) + internal \(r\); \(I=\mathcal{E}/(R+r)\); terminal \(V=\mathcal{E}-Ir\); open-circuit \(V\approx\mathcal{E}\); short-circuit \(I_{\mathrm{sc}}=\mathcal{E}/r\); \(V\)–\(I\) graph slope \(=r\).

| QB MC | Topic |
|-------|-------|
| *(Most QB items assume negligible \(r\))* | |
| **Q41** | Two bulbs with given \(V\) — infers source / divider (borderline) |

*No QB item in this bank explicitly gives \(\mathcal{E}\), \(r\), and asks for terminal \(V\) or \(I_{\mathrm{sc}}\) — internal resistance is mainly covered in the textbook here.*

---

### **Practical ammeters & voltmeters** *(Book 4: end of §21.6)*
**Covers:** Ideal A in series (\(R\approx0\)); ideal V in parallel (\(R\approx\infty\)); non-ideal meters alter readings; two layouts for measuring \(R\); voltmeter across named points; cell combinations for e.m.f.

| QB MC | Topic |
|-------|-------|
| **Q28** | Correct ammeter connection |
| **Q32** | Correct voltmeter connection |
| **Q33** | Identical cells — series/parallel/opposing e.m.f. |
| **Q4** | Moving voltmeter probe — which p.d. is measured |

*Ideal meter wiring is introduced earlier in §21.1–21.2; QB Q28/Q32/Q4 align with the practical-meter section.*

---

## Prior sections (context only — before §21.3)

| § | Book 4 topic | QB MC |
|---|--------------|-------|
| **§21.1** Current | \(I=Q/t\); conventional vs electron flow; charge conservation; ammeter in series | **Q23–Q27**, **Q28** |
| **§21.2** Voltage & energy | e.m.f. vs p.d.; \(V=E/Q\); energy conservation; hill diagram; voltmeter in parallel | **Q17**, **Q29–Q31**, **Q32**, **Q33** |

---

## Quick reference — progression summary

```
§21.3 Resistance          → Q7,13,16,18,22,34–35,42–46,56–57
§21.4 Resistor networks   → Q1–6,8–11,14–15,19–21,36–41,47–55,68–70
§21.5 Electrical power    → Q12,40,58–67
Short / open circuit      → Q36–37,39,48
§21.6 Internal resistance → (textbook; not strongly tested in this QB set)
Practical meters          → Q4,28,32,33
```

**Note on `circuits.tex` in your repo:** It follows the same Book 4 content but places **Power & energy last** (after meters). For teaching order aligned to the textbook, use the Book 4 sequence above (power → short circuit → internal resistance → meters).
